chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān narrated from Layth al-Murādī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat in the summer, during the short nights, namely Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night. He said: “Yes, good is what you considered, and good is what you did.”

key_terms.أَوَّلِ اللَّيْلِ: the beginning of the night, the time in question
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), here referring generally to ritual prayer
key_terms.الصَّيْفِ: summer, the season mentioned as the circumstance of the ruling
key_terms.اللَّيَالِي الْقِصَارِ: short nights, the practical condition affecting the timing
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer, the recommended worship being discussed
key_terms.صَنَعْتَ: you did, referring to the act already performed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night during short summer nights?
ai.summary: This hadith permits performing Salat al-Layl at the beginning of the night during summer when the nights are short. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام approves both the judgment and the practice, indicating flexibility in the timing of this recommended act of worship under such circumstances.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1379 - Abdullah ibn Muskan reported from Layth al-Muradi who said:

"I asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about praying the night prayer during the summer, when the nights are short, and performing it at the beginning of the night. Imam (as) said: 'Yes, what you have considered is good, and what you have done is good.'"
